# Full-network inference summary (generated by scripts/summarize_model.py)

ResNet-18 W8A8, **all 37 graph ops chained** (TRANSPOSE, 5 PAD, 20 CONV_2D, MAX_POOL, 8 ADD, AVG_POOL, FC), one image, bit-exact vs TFLite per op and on the logits. Dynamic instructions of the inference only (checksum/compare code excluded). Instruction counts, not cycles.

End-to-end B1->X1 = **6.45x** (GEMM-only B1->X1 = 7.02x): the non-GEMM operators are untouched by the extension, so Amdahl's law pulls the whole-model number below the kernel number.

## Cross-check: GEMM part of the chained run vs the stand-alone layer profile

| Config | chained GEMM insns (1 image) | sum of 21 layers (layers_profile.json) | diff |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| B0 | 12859666728 | 12859666728 | +0 |
| B1 | 7428739832 | 7428739832 | +0 |
| X0 | 1177736736 | 1177736736 | +0 |
| X1 | 1057733279 | 1057733279 | +0 |
| X2 | 714417433 | 714417433 | +0 |

The two profiles use the same `run_layer`/`gemm_*` source, so the GEMM part of the chained run must equal the sum of the stand-alone layers up to a few instructions of function prologue/register allocation (here at most 21 of ~10^9-10^10). A large diff would mean the chained run executes different kernel code than the verified layers.

## X2 (ldpi) and the T variants

X1->X2 = 1.416x, X1T->X2T = 1.416x (whole model, same loop order; only the pointer bumps are fused into the loads).  X1->X1T = 1.0084x (loop order only; its benefit is in the data cache, see cache_summary.md).
